4.3.4.7 Memory Protection and Pointer Type Parameters in RTE API
In a memory protected ECU, a SW-C from an untrusted partition might misuse the
transition to the trusted context to modify memory in another partition. This can occur
when a pointer to a different memory partition is passed from the untrusted partition to
the trusted context. The RTE shall avoid this misuse by at least checking the validity
of the address of the pointer, and, where possible, also checking the integrity of the
associated memory object.
[SWS_Rte_02752]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00210
⌈When a SW-C in an untrusted partition receives (OUT parameter) or provides (IN
parameter with composite data type) an ArgumentDataPrototype or Variable-
DataPrototype, it hands over a pointer to a memory object to an RTE API. The RTE
shall only forward this pointer to a trusted SW-C after it has checked that the whole
memory object is owned by the caller’s partition.⌋
[SWS_Rte_02753]
Upstream requirements: SRS_Rte_00210
⌈When a SW-C in an untrusted partition passes an ArgumentDataPrototype or
VariableDataPrototype, as a reference type to a SW-C in a trusted partition (
DATA_REFERENCE as an IN parameter), the RTE shall only check that the caller’s
partition owns the start address of the referenced memory.⌋
